frozen_question: Is there a reliable Egyptian museum or excavation object that combines a female figure with an intentional genital receptacle/opening and a removable or insertable phallus, and if not, how close do the surviving object classes come?

method_execution.TOPA_SPIDER: museum-record provenance crawl and bibliography backtracking
method_execution.FIVE_D_SPIRAL: object morphology -> chronology -> geography -> ritual function -> manufacturing technology -> contradiction return
method_execution.BEETLE_GRAZER: deduplicated object records and separated identical/parallel pieces from independent evidence
method_execution.TENET_REVERSE: started from the proposed assembled mechanism and searched backward for each physical prerequisite independently
method_execution.NEGATIVE_CONTROL: forbid combining two separate object classes into one archaeological mechanism without an explicit joined specimen or excavation association
method_execution.boundary: Named JANUS methods are used here as research logic and source-deduplication frames; no unavailable binary execution is claimed.

primary_object.findspot: Site 95, terracotta workshop, eastern edge of Naukratis
primary_object.description: Naked pregnant or fecundity female figure seated/squatting with legs wide apart. After removal from the mould and before firing, the vagina and anus were deliberately pierced in zones marked by raised edges.
primary_object.additional_iconography: Wreath with lotus buds described by the museum as having a phallic appearance.

parallel_object.relation: British Museum identifies it as an identical locally produced Naukratis example

object_lane_female_receptacle.interpretive_boundary: The museum record establishes intentional piercing of the vaginal region. It does not state that a detachable phallus was inserted into this opening.

naukratis_priapus.museum_source: British Museum Naukratis Project; object owned by Ashmolean Museum
naukratis_priapus.description: Terracotta Priapus figure with an empty socket explicitly identified as being for a removable phallus.

bes_stela.date: Ptolemaic or Roman Period, 4th century BCE-1st century CE
bes_stela.description: A hole remains where a large erect phallus would have been inserted.
bes_stela.ritual_context: Met compares the type with the Bes Chambers at the Anubeion at Saqqara, where large Bes reliefs with phalli were accompanied by smaller female figures and are interpreted in relation to incubation and fecundity.

geneva_priapus_control.museum: Musee d'art et d'histoire de Geneve
geneva_priapus_control.description: Ptolemaic/Roman Egyptian terracotta Priapus; museum record describes a circular orifice for an attached phallus.

brooklyn_fertility_figures.finding: Brooklyn Museum explicitly notes that nude Egyptian female figures once interpreted as symbolic concubines for male dead are now understood as fertility figures used by both men and women, often dedicated at shrines of Hathor and other goddesses by people seeking a child.

met_omphale.finding: The Metropolitan Museum notes that figures long called Baubo have recently been identified as Omphale; the exposed-genital iconography is associated with power over the womb, childbirth and rebirth after death.

rodin_baubo_literary_analogue.finding: Musee Rodin's Egyptian collection discussion notes the late literary Baubo tradition in which something may be inside the vagina, interpreted as possibly a phallic object or a child, while treating these figures broadly as fertility/protection/regeneration objects.

H1_independent_object_classes.definition: Pierced female fertility figures and detachable-phallus male/Bes/Priapus figures existed independently within overlapping ritual/material culture.

H2_composable_fertility_ritual_technolog.definition: Some pierced female figures may have accepted an inserted ritual element, potentially phallic, but the joined archaeological specimen has not yet been demonstrated.

H3_all_objects_are_merely_erotic.reason: Museum reinterpretations and explicit birth/fecundity functions show that exposed sexual anatomy can have fertility, protective and regenerative roles.

canonical_seal: 𓂸 THE TWO MECHANICAL HALVES EXIST: INTENTIONALLY PIERCED FEMALE FERTILITY FIGURES AND DETACHABLE PHALLIC COMPONENTS. THE JOIN BETWEEN THEM REMAINS A TEST, NOT A FACT. 𓂸
